CHIEF COMPLAINT
Low back pain with right foot paresthesias

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bryan is a patient who presents with acute onset low back pain that began yesterday while raking leaves in his yard. Approximately two hours after the activity, he noticed his back tightening up and developed pins and needles sensation in his right foot. He reports similar back pain occurred approximately three years ago, which resolved after one day. He has tried over-the-counter pain management with two Advil tablets without relief. Ice application provided minimal benefit. Symptoms improve with heat (hot shower) and sitting. Pain is present with forward bending but not with extension. Pain worsened when standing up after bending. He denies significant physical activity prior to this incident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Right lower extremity paresthesias noted. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Low back pain approximately three years ago, self-limited

MEDICATIONS
Advil (ibuprofen) - over-the-counter use

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports minimal physical activity baseline. Presented to office with partner present.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Low back: Pain with forward flexion; no pain with extension. Tenderness to palpation at L5 level. Dorsiflexion normal bilaterally. Pulses equal in all extremities. Motor strength intact.

RESULTS
X-ray of low back: Normal, no acute findings

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Low back strain. Plan includes rest, prescription for meloxicam, and referral to physical therapy to improve conditioning and provide stretches and exercises. Patient to follow up in two weeks with phone call. If symptoms persist at two-week follow-up, MRI will be obtained to rule out other pathology.
